why_seated: THE SCHOOL COMMENTARY. On De caelo II: Aristotle 'supposes for the present that the earth rests, which he will prove later', with Heraclides and Aristarchus reported as moving it daily (lect. 11 n. 2); the astronomers' suppositions need not be true, since the appearances might be saved some other way (lect. 17 n. 2); the indecisive phenomena answered with the lunar eclipse, and the Timaeus's ἰλλομένην read as binding, not motion (lect. 21 nn. 4–5).
